page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head at the top right, page number at the top left. Five marginal notes in the left margin, each beside its line. Catchword at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: jam agimus, idolum & simulacrum rectè distin-Thom. Aquin. 1. ad Cor. cap. 8. lect. 1.guit; quum {a}simulacrum dici tradit, quod sit ad similitudinem rei alicuius naturalis; idolum autem, ad nullius rei similitudinem, ut si corpori humano adda-tur caput equinum. Quod & ipse {b}alibi vidit correxitque: scribens, quarundam imaginum cultores idololatras dictos esse, quia latriæ cultum idolis, id est, imaginibus impendebant. Verum illud melius {c}Thomas quàm multa, qui tamen multa bene: aliud esse vocis significationem, aliud etymologiā; nec utramque semper eidem rei convenire. Quapropter etiamsi etymologiam simulacri in imaginem haud quadrare concederemus: sophisticè tamen Bellarminus inde conclusisset imagines non rectè vocari simulacra.

Testes Isidorus & Paulus Diaconus: autores eo judicio versati in scrutandis vocum etymologiis & significationibus, ut Bellarmini somnium [?] videantur facile fuisse amplexuri, si quis veterum anfam idoneam suppeditasset.

Origen. lib. 8. cap. 11.{d}Isidorus enim, utut in tradenda etymologia hu-ius fluet; ac simulacra dicta, vel quòd sunt similia, vel quòd simulata & conficta, scribat; significari tamen imaginem simulacro agnoscit absque omni controversia dicens; Fuerunt quidam viri fortes, aut urbium conditores, quibus mortuis homines, qui eos dilexerunt, simulacra finxerunt, ut haberent aliquod ex imaginum contemplatione solatium: item; Gentiles primum Prometheum simulacra hominum de luto finxisse perhibent, ab eo{que} natam esse arte simulacra & statuas fingedi; unde & poetæ ab eo homines primum fabulos esse confingunt figurate propter effigies. Infesto verbo, Pilat.{e}Paulus autem Diaconus effigies viriles & muliebres ex lana Compitalibus Romæ suspensas in compitis, ad placandos Lares, simulacra nuncupat. Quin etiam

page.notes: Printed page number at top left is partly worn; read as 364 with [?]. Marginal note letters (a–e) are inferred from the reference marks in the text. Note b ("Sum. contr. Gent. lib. 3. cap. 110") and note c ("In 1. 2. quæst. 91. art. 3. Quæst. disput. de potentia Dei quæst. 9. art. 3") are partly worn; the numbers are uncertain. The word after "Bellarmini" appears as "somnium" with a long-s initial and is doubtful. "fluet" is read from the broken word "hu-/stuet". "conficta" is doubtful. "fabulos" is partly worn; "muliebres" appears as "mulicbres" in the print. "fingedi" is kept as printed. The reference mark before "Paulus" looks like "c" in the image, but the margin note is "e"; it is transcribed as e. No signature visible.
